note: V(q) injective for q surjective; the quotient structure, when it exists, is unique. That the comodule axioms then hold automatically is not formalised.
Uniqueness of the induced structure when M' (x) A -> M (x) A is injective; existence iff delta(M') lands in M' (x) A.
The quotient condition needs no flatness (right exactness of (x) A); injectivity is used only for the induced structure on M'.
Proved: A flat, M' a direct factor, stability under sums (with no hypothesis). Not formalised: the case M'' flat (Tor) and finite intersections for A flat.

For an abstract monoid acting linearly (the points of a constant monoid): a quotient carries a compatible action iff the kernel is stable, and uniquely. The functor-of-points form needs comodules = actions of the monoid functor (not set up, as in Part01 19134).
Proved for A projective (a direct sum of f.g. projectives is projective); H acts by s.x = (id (x) s)(delta x) (act).
Smallest subcomodule = sub-H-module generated, for A projective; finite generation proved for A free (hull_fg).
Hx = span of the image of s |-> s.x is the smallest subcomodule containing x; finitely generated for A free.
For A free: every x lies in a f.g. subcomodule and f.g. subcomodules are stable under sums (a filtered union). The case A a direct sum of f.g. projectives that is not free is not done.
pi makes A a right comodule over itself; the left comodule axioms are the same coassociativity and counit laws.
One side: the smallest right sub-comodule of the regular comodule containing B (f.g. for A free). The two-sided sub-bicomodule is not formalised.
(B (x) A) cap (A (x) B) = B (x) B in A (x) A when A/B is flat; hence stable on both sides iff pi(B) in B (x) B.

Proved: every element of a coalgebra over a field lies in a finite-dimensional right subcomodule. The fundamental theorem (finite-dimensional subcoalgebras) and the dual pro-finite description of H are not formalised.
The step of the proof: the subalgebra generated by a subcoalgebra is a sub-bialgebra (a quotient monoid of finite type). The limit statement itself needs 23061.

The key step: if m_1..m_n generate A and pi(m_j) = sum m_i (x) a_ij, the matrix coefficients a_ij generate A, so k[End k^n] -> A is onto (closed immersion into End, into GL_n for a group). Existence of such a finite stable generating M (from 22476 over a field) is not assembled.

The antipode of a commutative Hopf algebra is an algebra map, so the subalgebra generated by an antipode-stable set is antipode-stable and G_i is a group. That M + sigma(M) is a stable subcoalgebra is not formalised.
As 23263: the image of k[M_n] -> A contains the coefficients, hence is everything.
(k, x) acting on k by multiplication: 0 acts by a non-invertible endomorphism.
The precise claim (the elements of M are coefficients of the representation, m_j = sum eps(m_i) a_ij) is the counit computation in coeff_generate.

Faithful special cases: a closed immersion of a noetherian affine scheme into itself is an isomorphism (surjective endomorphisms of noetherian rings are injective), and the finite step of the arithmetic proof. The general statement (EGA IV 17.9.6) is not formalised.
The argument on points: a finite monoid that embeds in a group is a group. The scheme statement depends on 24998.
Over every k' != 0, a monoid map (k', x) -> group is never injective.
The pairing and the induced V(A) (x)_O V(B) -> V(A (x) B).

The 'only if' is false: over k = Z, A = Z/2, B = Z/3 (neither projective), both sides vanish at every k', so the morphism is an isomorphism. The board (26115) says 'equality only if A or B is projective of finite type' too, so the slip may be Grothendieck's (oral) for 'equality if'. The 'if' direction is not formalised here.

correction.old: is an isomorphism only if $A$ or $B$ is finitely generated projective over $k$.
correction.new: is an isomorphism if $A$ or $B$ is finitely generated projective over $k$, but not in general.

note: The direction morphism N -> A (x) B gives a pairing; the converse (every bilinear pairing comes from a unique morphism) is not formalised.
delta(u) = u o mu; on points delta(x) = x (box) x.

The multiplication is recovered from delta (linear forms with values in commutative k-algebras separate points, via the trivial square-zero extension). That every natural coalgebra structure on V(A) comes from an algebra structure (Yoneda on S(A)) is not formalised.
Each axiom of mu is equivalent to the dual axiom of delta, stated pointwise on V(A)(k').
The convolution law on Dist(X) induces the law of X; compatibility with delta (delta(u*v) = delta u * delta v) is not formalised.
Associativity of the convolution law from coassociativity is Mathlib; the converse (laws on Dist compatible with delta come from X) is not formalised.

As Part01 19134/19931: one direction only, the action s.x of Hom(A,k) on a comodule and s.(t.x) = (s*t).x (act, act_act, act_counit) is a module structure over Dist(G)(k); the functor-of-points equivalence is not formalised.
Mathlib lacks the linearly topologised (pseudo-compact) dual H = lim A_alpha^vee of a coalgebra and continuous H-modules.
The O-submodule of distributions vanishing on a power of I; that it is a subalgebra is not formalised.
Dist = O (+) Dist^+ (u = u(1).1 + v, v(1) = 0, uniquely). The Lie algebra of G inside it, with the commutator bracket, is not formalised (Mathlib has no Lie algebra of a group scheme).
Mathlib has no restricted (p-)Lie algebras and no Lie algebra of a group scheme.
The splitting O (+) Dist^+; generation by the Lie algebra in characteristic 0 (Cartier) is not formalised.
The product of (k^Gamma)^vee transposed from (Delta f)(g,h) = f(gh) sends the dual basis e_g, e_h to e_gh: the group algebra.
Representations of an abstract group Gamma = k[Gamma]-module structures; the identification of representations of the constant group scheme with those of Gamma is not formalised.
I^2 = I for any group Gamma (I generated by the idempotent 1 - delta_1).

Points over a domain with 2 != 0: mu_2 = {1,-1}; characteristic 2: -1 = 1 and 1+eps is a non-trivial point of mu_2 over k[eps]. The isomorphism of schemes and the hyperalgebra computation x^2 = x are not formalised.
For a comodule V over k[M]: the p_m are orthogonal projectors, finitely many p_m x are nonzero and x = sum p_m x.
One direction: an action gives the grading (each x is uniquely a finite sum of x_m with p_m x_m = x_m). The converse (grading -> comodule) is not formalised.
On V_m, delta x = x (x) e^m, so a point g acts by the unit g(e^m) = chi_m(g).
Object level only (29057); morphisms and the equivalence of categories are not formalised.
chi_m chi_m' = chi_(m+m'); tensor products of comodules are not set up.
The affine base S = Spec k; quasi-coherent modules over a general S are not done.
M_S as the coproduct of copies of S in Mathlib's schemes; commutation with finite products not formalised.
Mathlib instance: a finite coproduct of affine schemes is affine (the 'if'); the converses (affine or of finite type implies M finite) are not formalised.
On points D(M)(R) = Hom(M, R^x) (Part01.D, represented by k[M]) and maps M_S' -> X are maps M -> X(S'); the sheaf Hom_gr(M_S, G_m) is not set up.
Maps out of M_S' = maps M -> Hom(S', X) (coproduct); the compatibility with composition laws is not formalised.

Affine S = Spec R: a homomorphism D(M) -> G_m (a group-like element of R[M]) is a family of orthogonal idempotents with sum 1 (a partition of S into open-closed pieces). The converse and the general S are not formalised.
Affine connected S (only idempotents 0, 1): group-like elements of R[M] are the e^m, for a unique m.
Full faithfulness over a domain (Mathlib); essential surjectivity is the definition of diagonalizable.
Mathlib has no abelian varieties nor the sheaf Ext^1(G, G_m).
Affine version: A finite and projective (locally free of finite type) over the base ring.
Affine base, module-finite presentation: finite projective iff finite, flat and finitely presented.
D(G) defined pointwise by monoid maps to (O, x); G_m its largest subgroup (Part01).

Module-level biduality A = A^vee-vee for f.g. projective A and the identification of D(G)(k) with algebra maps A^vee -> k; representability of D(G) by a finite locally free monoid scheme and G = D(D(G)) are not assembled.
The section u of a monoid map G -> (A^1, x) (a bialgebra map k[N] -> A) is group-like; the converse is not formalised.
Both directions, the converse for A projective (linear forms separate A (x) A).

Algebra maps H -> k' to commutative k' factor uniquely through H^ab; 'not necessarily locally free' is not formalised.
Module-level involution A |-> A^vee; the self-duality of the Hopf axioms is not formalised.

mu_p = D(Z/p) on points and mu_p infinitesimal (Part01); D(mu_p) = Z/p not formalised.

Etale implies reduced with separable residue fields (even geometrically reduced), but not conversely: A^1_k is geometrically reduced and not etale. The board (2844) has the implication only, so the equivalence is the edition's.

Several components can pass over a geometrically normal point (X = Spec C over R: two components over its single point); what holds is that each point above it lies on one component (normal local rings are domains), which is what x not in Sigma needs. The board (5696) says 'local rings of X' are domains', so the slip is the edition's.
